title: Restore extension module loading inside the compiled runtime
before: At parent 53d9e61bac3408b4ff6b4ccf9dd49e1c4c9640b1, the extension loader exposed the host package to compiled-runtime extensions through a lazy require of the public index. The public index simultaneously re-exported loader functions, creating a loader-to-index-to-loader cycle. The compiled-runtime virtual module table omitted the agent-core package, the development alias table omitted the same package, and the root compilation dependency graph resolved @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.2. after: At 843f2352518cb75343f9e6e47bb86f708e1f4769, loader functions are no longer re-exported from the public index, allowing the loader to statically import the initialized public API without a circular dependency. The root package and lockfile select @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.5, described by the commit and changelog as bundling the transformation support required by the compiled runtime. Extension discovery and SDK/CLI call sites continue importing loader operations through the internal extensions module.
diff: The implementation removes createExtensionRuntime, discoverAndLoadExtensions, and loadExtensions from the package-root value exports; replaces the lazy public-API getter and runtime require with a static index import and direct virtual-module entry; adds agent-core to both compiled-runtime virtual modules and development aliases; and upgrades the root jiti dependency and lockfile resolution from 2.6.2 to 2.6.5. title: Make callback delivery lazy-safe and force reload lifecycle-symmetric
before: At parent eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4, module-level hook and middleware invocation and presence checks directly queried the process plugin manager without ensuring discovery. Processes that did not import the component whose side effect triggered discovery could therefore report no callback or silently skip delivery. Separately, full unload cleared manager-local hooks without restoring configuration-owned shell hooks, and it removed legacy platform registrations but did not deregister tool names tracked outside the ownership ledger, allowing missing configuration hooks and stale global tools after force reload.
after: At 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be, callback delivery entry points obtain a delivery manager that joins in-flight background discovery and performs discovery when necessary while preserving compatibility with manager test doubles. Full unload also deregisters tracked tool names not represented by tool ownership records. After a successful forced discovery sweep, configuration-owned shell hooks are rebuilt from current configuration; restoration failures are logged and do not invalidate the completed reload.
diff: The change adds a lazy-discovery delivery helper and routes module-level invoke_hook, invoke_middleware, has_hook, and has_middleware through it; adds a legacy-tool cleanup sweep during unload-all while excluding ownership-ledger tools; adds configuration-hook re-registration that resets registration idempotence and reloads configuration; invokes that reconciliation only after successful force rediscovery; and adds focused tests for lazy delivery, gate behavior, mock-manager compatibility, shell-hook restoration, fail-open restoration, and stale-tool cleanup. The commit modifies agent/shell_hooks.py, hermes_cli/plugins.py, and tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py with 282 insertions and 5 deletions.

commit.subject: fix(plugins): hook delivery parity + symmetric force-reload (#64178)
commit.body_excerpt:
Salvaged from PR #64188 (@Bartok9), re-reviewed against the #64229
ownership ledger (landed in #84923).

Delivery parity (survived):
- Module-level invoke_hook/invoke_middleware/has_hook/has_middleware
  lazily run plugin discovery via _delivery_manager(), so surfaces that
  never import model_tools (dashboards, TUI slash workers, query mode,
  cron, gateway platform events) deliver plugin callbacks instead of
  silently dropping them (#50776, #67597, #67890, #50937).
- _delivery_manager() joins any in-flight background discovery first and
  tolerates test doubles that monkeypatch get_plugin_manager().

Symmetric force-reload (survived):
- agent/shell_hooks.py gains re_register_config_hooks(); the force branch
  of discover_and_load() calls it after a successful sweep, restoring
  config.yaml shell hooks that the ledger-driven unload wiped but cannot
  restore (they are config-owned, not plugin-owned) (#60036).
- unload(plugin=None) now sweeps pre-ledger _plugin_tool_names entries
  out of the process-global tools.registry, mirroring the platform-name
  sweep that already existed, so zombie tools cannot survive a force
  reload in long-lived pre-ledger processes (#60050).

title: Resolve extension uninstall requests by installed name or recorded source
before: At parent commit 0534ca74d4e67b00ed51e9f8bf568efc3ecaf834, uninstallExtension treated its argument strictly as an extension name. It required an exact case-sensitive match against installed.config.name, rejected source URLs or paths even when recorded in installation metadata, and then used the supplied argument directly for enablement removal, storage deletion, and uninstall telemetry. The CLI likewise described the positional argument only as an extension name.
after: At commit 2d406ffc755f79dc903c6993aae03150e1678dc0, the uninstall boundary accepts an identifier that may be either the configured extension name or installMetadata.source. It searches loaded user extensions using case-insensitive equality, safely skips absent metadata, resolves a match to the canonical configured name, and uses that canonical name for enablement removal, directory deletion, and telemetry. The CLI advertises name or source path input. Unknown identifiers, including source identifiers for installations without metadata, fail without deleting an extension.
diff: The change renamed the core input concept from extensionName to extensionIdentifier; replaced the name-only existence check with lookup by normalized configured name or normalized recorded source; retained the resolved config.name as the canonical lifecycle key; generalized the not-found error; updated CLI argument documentation; and added tests proving source-URL deletion and canonical-name telemetry while preserving name-based deletion, unrelated installations, and safe failure when metadata is absent.

title: Detect extension changes and reconcile the live runtime without restarting the session
before: At parent 271664b34b15c55366815ccb11f3eeb0698b8ad5, extension-manager operations could directly refresh MCP tools, skill and subagent caches, and hierarchical memory, but the interactive session had no extension-package filesystem watcher, no shared stale/reload state, no manual package reload command, and no content-only refresh path. Out-of-band edits to installed or linked extension commands, skills, agents, hooks, manifests, context, or package topology therefore were not reconciled into the running session. Configured hooks also had no reload operation that preserved agent-scoped hooks and enabled state.
after: At 151d2694136da5d89c8133bbdb8c08897ae2c107, the CLI watches installed and active linked extension roots, classifies command/skill/agent edits for debounced automatic content refresh and package-level edits for explicit reload, suppresses watcher noise during manager-owned mutations, and coordinates concurrent changes through session-scoped refresh state. A manual reload command rebuilds the extension cache, the multi-component runtime, and slash commands from a coherent snapshot. Core refresh now covers MCP, LSP, skills, subagents, configured hooks, and hierarchical memory with explicit failure propagation, while configured-hook reload preserves agent-scoped hooks and enabled state and rolls back on failure.
diff: The implementation adds ExtensionFileWatcher, ExtensionRefreshState, CLI runtime reload helpers, a manual reload slash command, startup/UI wiring, localized feedback, and tests. It adds native id-paired mutation lifecycle events to the extension manager, expands the core runtime refresh contract to MCP/LSP/hooks, and adds transactional configured-hook reload. The watcher uses conservative path classification, linked-root discovery, bootstrap watching, symlink avoidance, stale-file tracking, generation guards, and mutation suppression. Content refresh is debounced and serialized with a bounded pending-pass loop; package refresh rebuilds cache, runtime components, commands, and a capability summary.

evidence_units.claim: The change adds dedicated watcher, refresh-state, runtime-reload, reload-command, and associated test modules, while modifying startup, UI command processing, the extension manager, core runtime refresh, and hook registry/system integration.

The watcher observes the installed-extension directory and active linked sources, avoids following symlinks, ignores initial events, waits for writes to settle, and classifies commands/skills/agents as automatic refresh while manifests and hooks are package-stale.

When the extension directory does not yet exist, a parent bootstrap watcher detects its creation, marks state stale, and defers watcher restart to a microtask; watcher generations reject buffered events from stopped instances.

Shared refresh state deduplicates package-stale notifications, blocks content refresh while package reload is required, records changes arriving during reload, re-emits deferred work after success, and keeps reload-needed state on failure.

Mutation notification suppression is depth-counted, remains active briefly after settlement, supports synchronous and promise-returning operations, and invokes settlement only after overlapping suppressions end.

The extension manager emits native start/end mutation events with unique ids, wraps runtime-relevant mutations in try/finally, and the watcher pairs suppression callbacks by id before restarting its roots after mutations settle.
Content-only refresh refreshes the extension cache, skill cache, subagent cache, and slash commands; independent legs settle before aggregated errors are reported, and safe mode skips the operation.

The slash-command processor debounces content events, serializes refreshes, records a pending pass for changes arriving during execution, stops if package reload becomes necessary, and bounds repeated passes.
Manual package reload rejects safe mode, refreshes the extension cache and full runtime, rebuilds slash commands, and summarizes active extension capabilities.

The manual reload command marks reload start, invokes package reload with command rebuilding, clears state on success, preserves reload-needed state on failure, and returns localized success or error feedback.

Core runtime refresh requires MCP reconciliation first, then reconciles LSP, settles skills/subagents/hooks in parallel, attempts hierarchical-memory refresh, and surfaces hook and LSP failures individually or as an aggregate.
In the parent, core refresh restarted MCP through the tool registry, refreshed only skills and subagents, and attempted hierarchical-memory refresh; it did not reconcile LSP or configured hooks.

Configured-hook reload snapshots prior entries and enabled states, retains agent-scoped entries, rebuilds configured hooks, restores matching enabled states, and restores the entire previous registry if rebuilding throws.
Interactive startup creates one session-scoped refresh state, omits the watcher in bare or safe mode, starts the watcher otherwise, and supplies that shared state to UI consumers.

Watcher tests cover installed and linked roots, path classification, inactive-root exclusion, ignored files, bootstrap watching, mutation-settlement restart, stale-generation rejection, overlapping id pairing, and cleanup of pending suppressions.
Refresh-state tests verify deduplication, mutation suppression, post-mutation windows, changes during reload, stale-over-content priority, failed-reload state, and overlapping suppression settlement.

Runtime helper tests verify full package refresh and capability counts, safe-mode rejection, content refresh of all independent legs, continued settlement before failure reporting, and absent subagent-manager handling.

Core refresh tests verify ordering and coverage, MCP failure propagation, LSP partial and thrown failures, continued independent refresh, delayed hook failure propagation, aggregate failures, and best-effort memory refresh.
Hook tests prove configured reload preserves agent-scoped hooks and enabled state and restores all prior hooks on failure.

UI processor tests prove debounced automatic content refresh, visible failure feedback, suppression while package reload is needed, retry messaging after package reload failure, and cancellation when manual reload starts.

The committed test suite provides direct behavioral oracles for classification, lifecycle coordination, component reconciliation, error propagation, and hook-state preservation; no execution result for these tests is present in the supplied evidence.

candidate_atomics.title: Coordinate reload state and suppress self-generated watcher events
candidate_atomics.description: Use session-scoped state and id-paired mutation events to deduplicate notifications, retain concurrent changes, and avoid reacting to programmatic writes.

candidate_atomics.title: Rebuild the extension runtime from one coherent snapshot

candidate_atomics.title: Reload configured hooks without discarding session hooks

candidate_workflows.name: reconcile-live-extension-changes
candidate_workflows.title: Reconcile live extension changes at the narrowest safe scope
candidate_workflows.description: Watch extension-owned files, classify each change, coordinate concurrent lifecycle activity, automatically refresh content-only capabilities, and require a coherent package reload when broader runtime state may have changed.

workflow_graph.goal: Keep a running interactive session consistent with extension files while avoiding unsafe partial application, watcher feedback loops, and loss of session-scoped runtime state.
when_to_use: A long-lived process loads extensible capabilities from files that users or development tools can edit outside the process.
Some extension changes can be refreshed locally, while manifests, hooks, topology, or referenced configuration require a coherent whole-package rebuild.
Programmatic extension mutations and filesystem notifications may overlap or echo one another.
anti_goals: Do not hot-apply arbitrary or unknown extension files.
Do not treat security-sensitive hook edits as content-only refreshes.
Do not change extension discovery, installation-source, marketplace, or conversion semantics as part of reload coordination.
Do not follow extension-provided symlinks into arbitrary external paths.
Do not hide MCP, LSP, hook, or aggregated content-refresh failures behind a success message.
not_applicable_when: The process has no persistent runtime state or always restarts after extension changes.
The session is in bare or safe mode where extensions or reload are disabled.
All extension changes are already performed through one transactional owner and no out-of-band filesystem edits are supported.
The host cannot identify semantic file classes or provide subsystem refresh APIs with validation oracles.
inputs: Active extension metadata and roots, including linked sources
Filesystem event kind and absolute changed path
Session-scoped refresh state and event channel
workflow_graph.entry_state: The running session may hold extension cache, commands, skills, agents, hooks, external servers, and context that no longer match files on disk, or a manager-owned mutation may be writing those files.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every observed relevant change is either applied through a completed bounded content refresh or represented by a visible package-reload requirement; after successful package reload, runtime components and commands reflect one refreshed extension snapshot, while concurrent or failed changes remain retryable.

steps.condition: A filesystem event occurs under an installed root, an active linked source, or a tracked referenced file.
steps.validation: The event resolves to automatic content refresh, package-stale, or ignored using tests for each supported path class.

steps.condition: Always for admitted automatic or package-stale events, and around manager-owned mutations and manual reloads.
steps.validation: State tests show deduplication, priority, deferred-event retention, overlap-safe suppression, and retry state after failure.

steps.condition: The change is limited to commands, skills, or agents; safe mode is off; no package-stale flag exists.
steps.validation: All content cache and command legs settle, another bounded pass runs for concurrent changes, and any errors are aggregated and shown.

steps.condition: A package reload reaches the configured-hook refresh leg.
steps.validation: Agent-scoped hooks and enabled states survive successful reload, and the prior complete registry survives failure.

steps.condition: The change affects package topology, manifests, hooks, context, enablement, install metadata, or referenced runtime configuration, or automatic content refresh reports failure and the user retries with package reload.
steps.validation: Cache, runtime subsystems, and commands are rebuilt; material partial failures are returned; success reports active capability counts and clears stale state.

validation_ladder: Unit-test path classification for installed roots, linked roots, tracked referenced files, ignored files, topology creation/removal, and missing manifests.
Unit-test refresh state for deduplication, overlapping mutation suppression, changes during reload, stale-over-content priority, and failure retryability.
Unit-test content refresh for cache and command coverage, independent-leg settlement, aggregated errors, safe-mode behavior, debounce, and cancellation.
Unit-test configured-hook reload for session-hook preservation, enabled-state preservation, and transactional rollback.
Unit-test package runtime reconciliation for MCP-first behavior, LSP and hook failure propagation, best-effort legs, command rebuilding, and summary counts.

Exercise the interactive session by editing each supported file class and confirming either immediate capability visibility or a package-reload prompt, followed by successful reload or actionable failure feedback.
stop_conditions: Stop automatic refresh when the session enters safe or bare mode.
Stop content-only reconciliation and require package reload when package-stale state is set.
Stop classifying unknown files as reloadable unless a semantic owner and validation oracle are added.
Stop and retain retry-needed state when a material package reload leg fails.
Stop repeated automatic passes at the configured bound and surface the noisy-change failure.
unresolved_or_deferred: No test execution or CI result was supplied or run for this extraction; validation evidence is the committed test code and its asserted oracles.
Per-extension incremental external-server restart remains intentionally deferred; the implementation uses existing global reconciliation entry points.
Unknown extension files remain ignored until explicitly assigned a safe lifecycle class.
The extraction does not establish behavior outside the interactive CLI startup path.

The exact downstream recovery behavior after partial MCP or LSP reconciliation depends on subsystem implementations outside this bounded episode.
No cross-repository peer workflows or untouched holdout result were supplied, so this episode supports Actions and an issue Workflow only, not promotion of a universal Resolution Pattern.
